title: Same stochastic estimate. Less work?
audience: Adults interested in numerical computing; not made for kids
premise: An analyst tries to compute a stochastic estimate; cancelling repeated intermediate terms reduces work while preserving the answer, but setup and rounding limit the benefit.
novelty: New original explanatory animation of this computational study, not a newly discovered mathematical method.
closest_episode_difference: Earlier Strata and MLX clips trace implementation defects. This episode explains equal estimators and the difference between algebraic savings and statistical accuracy; no vendor defect.

scenes.title: Same path. Same estimate.
scenes.voice: Can the same stochastic estimate take less work? We tested two equal formulas on the same Brownian paths.
scenes.visual: One observed path sends identical nodes into two calculation lanes.

scenes.title: Cancel repeated work
scenes.voice: One repeats local products. The other cancels intermediate terms, keeping one final cube.
scenes.visual: Adjacent positive and negative cubic endpoint terms pair and disappear; the terminal cube and trapezoid sum remain.

scenes.title: A measured local speedup
scenes.voice: Our small Python benchmark ran about three times faster, with unchanged mathematical error. Including test data preparation made the gain smaller.
scenes.visual: Two timing bars converge to the same J; exact labels distinguish computation from accounted harness costs.

scenes.title: Reuse has trade-offs
scenes.voice: Reusing moments also helped batches, but slowed single requests and could worsen rounding.
scenes.visual: A common cache feeds several polynomial requests; one request pays setup alone; a rounding warning remains visible.

scenes.title: Known methods, tested carefully
scenes.voice: These are optimizations of known methods, not a new Itô integral or a correction to Black Scholes. The code and limitations are linked below.
scenes.visual: An evidence folder shows code, raw results and negative controls; the original integral remains unchanged.
